links.outcome: Discrimination (AUC) of externally trained sepsis models before vs after retraining on local GOSH data
links.effect: Retraining on GOSH data restored discrimination (AUC range 0.69–0.86); Gradient Boosting AUC 0.86 vs 0.87 at CHOP; KNN 0.80 vs 0.79; DeLong significant gains across all classifiers (p < 0.001).
links.quote: Retraining on GOSH data restored discrimination (AUC range 0.69–0.86), with Gradient Boosting (AUC 0.86 vs AUC 0.87 at CHOP) and KNN (AUC 0.80 vs AUC 0.79 at CHOP) models performing comparably to their CHOP benchmarks.

links.outcome: Performance drop when transferring the neonatal-trained model to mixed ICU population
links.effect: Models with strong CHOP neonatal discrimination showed reduced performance on mixed GOSH ICU population, attributed to domain and population shift.
links.quote: Models achieved strong discrimination on the CHOP neonatal cohort but demonstrated reduced performance when transferred to the mixed GOSH ICU population, reflecting anticipated domain and population shift.

links.effect: CHOP-trained models had reduced performance when transferred to mixed GOSH ICU; no transferred AUC reported.
links.quote: Models achieved strong discrimination on the CHOP neonatal cohort but demonstrated reduced performance when transferred to the mixed GOSH ICU population, reflecting anticipated domain and population shift.

links.effect: ICU cohort and baseline demographic differences introduced domain shift limiting direct transfer; no numeric effect reported.
links.quote: ICU cohort and baseline demographic differences between CHOP and GOSH introduced domain shift that limited direct model transfer.
